clips_intro: Each clip passed the automatic motion check and a fresh independent reviewer (cause and effect, what a stranger sees with the sound off, whether it shows the line) before this page. The stills are the approved start and end frames; J2 shows its new WHOOP start frame.

clips.name: Thumbs-up, then nods off (short 4)
clips.about: Made on your Google subscription. The short uses its first 4.3 seconds; after about 6.6 seconds the take snaps back to its end frame, so that part is not used. Slightly darker mids and a bit more colour to sit beside your footage.

clips.name: Smart ring close-up (short 5 opener)
clips.about: Made on your upgraded Google subscription, from the approved start frame. Two earlier paid takes made from the start and end frames clenched the hand into a fist and failed review, so they were thrown out. The hand lifts with its fingers open and the ring catches the light, then it settles. Seconds 0.6 to 4.3 of the take.

clips.name: Ring and WHOOP on one hand (short 5)
clips.about: The band is now a WHOOP: knit strap, square screenless sensor on top of the wrist, in every frame. The end frame shown here (a loose fist) passed its checks, but Veo could not close the hand into it without a finger flicking up (four paid takes), so the clip uses the WHOOP start frame with the open hand lifting slightly, the same motion as the ring opener. Made on the paid service before your upgrade.

decided: The WHOOP band (J2): Codex edited the start frame you approved and replaced only the band: a black knit strap with the small square sensor on top of the wrist, no screen, no logo. The automatic frame check and a separate reviewer both passed it.

J2's motion changed (overrule it): a hand turning palm-up would hide the WHOOP sensor in exactly the end frame you asked to fix, so I made the end frame a relaxed fist instead (it passed both checks). Veo could not close the hand into that fist without a finger flicking up, four takes in a row, so the clip uses the new WHOOP start frame with the open hand lifting slightly, the motion that worked for the ring.

J2 plays over the second sentence only (0:16.3 to 0:20.6): "wrist-based or a finger-based sleep tracker" is the line the ring-and-WHOOP hand shows, and the take is 6 seconds, too short for the whole 6.8 seconds you approved. You stay on camera for "Oura Ring and WHOOP are my top two options".
J2 framing: the crop keeps the WHOOP sensor above the captions, so for about two seconds the raised fingertips run off the top of the picture. A reviewer checked it and called it fine for a close-up.
Where the AI clips came from: K1 and the final J1 on your Google subscription (60 credits). J2 and two rejected J1 takes on the paid Veo service before your upgrade, while the credits were out.

AI labels: every AI clip carries the AI-GENERATED chip. K1 and J1 have it top left on the background; J2 has it on the empty desk at lower left. The automatic label-placement tool cannot read a close-up of a hand (it marked the whole bed sheet as a person), so I placed J2's by measuring the hand on ten frames.
Colour: the three clips came out brighter than your studio footage (a sunny kitchen, white sheets, a light desk), so each gets slightly darker mid-tones and a little more colour.
K1 uses its first 4.3 seconds. After about 6.6 seconds the take snaps back toward its end frame, so that part is never used.

Spend: $4.80 on the paid Veo service, all for short 5: $1.20 for two ring takes (both rejected) and $3.60 for five WHOOP takes (four rejected). That is more than the $1.60 to $3.20 I estimated, but inside the $5 limit for one short. Short 4 cost nothing (subscription credits).

One tool fix for every session: two paid Veo runs started at the same moment overwrote each other's records, and one rejected take's file was lost (the spend log stayed correct). The tool now locks its job file and never reuses a take's file name.
Upload settings: shorts 3, 4 and 5 now contain AI clips, so the setup task turns on YouTube's and TikTok's AI label for those three (recorded in the batch notes).
